artifacts.notes: The work occupies one wiki page, current revision 253468 at retrieval, which is the preface and the whole of the questions. artifacts.rights_basis: Jerome's Latin is of the fourth century and Migne's printing is of 1845, so the text beneath these bytes is in the public domain everywhere. The bytes themselves are the wiki source of a Latin Wikisource transcription, and Latin Wikisource contributions are licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 — a condition on the contributors' markup rather than on Migne's text under it. The exact bytes are therefore hashed and recorded but not retained here, and only the printed Latin reaches the tracked derivative, stripped of every template, link, heading and column marker the contributors and the encoder added.

work.author: Jerome
work.description: Not a commentary but a collection of notes, each on one verse, comparing the Latin and Greek of a passage with the Hebrew behind it and with Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion. Jerome's preface answers his critics before he begins and tells the reader to look for no eloquence in it. The questions run from Genesis 1:2 to Genesis 49, passing over whatever raises nothing in the Hebrew, which is most of the book.
work.title: Liber quaestionum hebraicarum in Genesim
